stories.title: Steelers' soft zone scheme could have big problems with Bengals QB Joe Burrow
stories.summary: Pittsburgh will also need to figure out how to slow down Cincinnati running back Chase Brown, who's beaten them up in recent matchups.
stories.detailText: The Pittsburgh Steelers will travel to face the Cincinnati Bengals in an NFL Week 10 rematch that has major implications for the AFC North race. The former prevailed by a 30-27 margin when these teams first faced off in September in a back-and-forth affair that ended with the Pittsburgh defense stopping a late bid by quarterback Joe Burrow and the Bengals offense to tie the game or take the lead late. The winner will take a one-game lead in the division. If the Steelers win, they’ll own the head-to-head tiebreaker at the end of the season. If the Bengals win, they’ll enjoy a favorable schedule to stay one step ahead of first-year coach Mike McCarthy’s team. Here’s USA TODAY’s guide on what to look for in the matchup, which will air nationally on NBC’s “Sunday Night Football.” Required reading: 3 questions that will make or break the second half of the Steelers season Will Joe Burrow crack the soft zone scheme? The Bengals star came as close as anyone has all season to solving Pittsburgh defensive coordinator Patrick Graham’s revamped system designed to avoid getting beat on long pass plays. Burrow completed 28 of 37 passes for 282 yards and three touchdowns during the initial Week 3 matchup. He found four different receivers for gains of at least 20 yards, and two of his three scoring tosses came from outside the red zone. The Steelers have done a nice job of keeping the play in front of them since, a major reason they’re allowing just 14.25 points per game during their current four-game winning streak. Burrow has the receiving talent to challenge that success once again. Ja’Marr Chase has 647 yards and seven touchdowns already in 2026. Counterpart Tee Higgins has been even better with 758 yards and six scores. It should be quite the battle of wits, with Burrow likely holding the advantage as he gets the start at home at Paycor Stadium. Which Aaron Rodgers will we see? As good as Burrow was against Pittsburgh in that first meeting, the Steelers quarterback was even more efficient. He averaged 8.6 yards per attempt in piling up a total of 292 and three touchdowns, plus a tipped interception. The big plays came early and often. Running back Jaylen Warren took the first pass of the game for a 30-yard gain en route to piling up 176 yards from scrimmage. Tight end Darnell Washington had a 47-yard catch. Receiver Roman Wilson added a 38-yard touchdown. Tight end Pat Freiermuth and receiver Ben Skowronek added receptions of at least 20 yards of their own. It was a sharp contrast to what we’ve seen from McCarthy’s offense since. Amid injuries to Wilson and fellow receiver Michael Pittman Jr., the playcalling has learned into the running game with Warren and a short-and-quick passing attack that’s decent at moving the chains but not so great at piling up yardage in bunches. It will therefore be interesting to see to what degree McCarthy tries to stick with what worked against the Bengals versus what’s worked against the rest of the schedule so far. Can Chase Brown find holes? The Steelers defense has smothered opposing running games. It’s allowing an average of just 55 yards on the ground over the past four games. The Bengals running back, however, has been kryptonite for the group over his past four outings against Pittsburgh. He’s averaged 6.25 yards per carry and totaled 338 yards over the span, which has forced the Steelers to respect the run while seeking principally to slow Burrow, Chase and Higgins. Pittsburgh has benefitted from being able to make opposing offenses one dimensional, so keep an eye on the amount of balance Brown is able to give Cincinnati in this one. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Steelers' soft zone scheme could have big problems with Bengals QB Joe Burrow

stories.title: Don Willard to serve as the head referee for 2 NFL games on same day after league switches up assignments
stories.summary: It is unclear whether Willard and his crew will make history on Sunday.
stories.detailText: NFL referee Don Willard is set to serve as the head referee for two NFL games in the same day. It is not readily known whether this has happened before, according to The Athletic . He's being pressed into double duty because of the league scrambling to reassign officiating crews due to travel issues caused by Friday's unprecedented four-hour nationwide ground stop for domestic flights in the United States. This impacted travel plans across sports leagues, including a college football game between Ole Miss and Oklahoma, which was moved to Sunday . It didn't impact start times for any NFL games, but it did force the league to switch up some referee assignments. Willard and his crew — umpire Terry Killens, field judge Jabir Walker and side judge Justin Larrew — will begin the day calling the Miami Dolphins-Indianapolis Colts game, set to kick off at 1 p.m. ET in Indiana. After the game, Willard and Co. will then drive 110 miles to Cincinnati, Ohio, to call the Pittsburgh Steelers-Cincinnati Bengals game for Week 10's "Sunday Night Football," which begins at 8:20 p.m. ET. While only three officiating crew changes were needed, one could be for the history books. Willard has been an NFL official for nine years, including officiating six playoff games. He typically serves as a side judge for Scott Novak's crew. The NFL made the reassignments based on driving distance from officials' hometowns. The other two moves were to have umpire Barry Anderson take over for Alex Moore in the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Tennessee Titans, while Duane Heydt steps in for Shawn Smith in the Carolina Panthers-New Orleans Saints NFC South battle. Originally, Carl Cheffers was supposed to referee the Miami-Indianapolis game, while Clete Blakeman was supposed to lead the Pittsburgh-Cincinnati game. Willard will now be the head referee for both games.

stories.title: Keionte Scott receives his first NFL fine from Buccaneers vs. Bears in Week 9
stories.summary: Keionte Scott got hit with his very first NFL fine for unnecessary roughness vs. the Bears.
stories.detailText: Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images | Getty Images The Buccaneers lost a 27-24 heartbreaker to the Chicago Bears in Week 9, and cornerback Keionte Scott lost $6,540 to a NFL fine for unnecessary roughness/use of the helmet in that loss. The fine was assessed for a second-quarter tackle of Bears WR Kalif Raymond. stories.title: Bills trending up, trending down: The players who will decide game at Jets
stories.summary: Which Bills should be decisive in the Week 10 divisional matchup against the Jets?
stories.detailText: The Bills lead the NFL in points per game (32.0) and total yards per game (386.4), and they head to MetLife at 7-1 on a four-game winning streak. The Jets are 2-7 and have lost four in a row, which makes this look like a game that plays itself. Joe Brady spent the week telling reporters that records can mislead in this league, and New York gives him some material: the NFL’s fifth-highest pressure rate (39.2 percent), 22 sacks, and a rookie in David Bailey, the second overall pick, who is tied for fourth in sacks (7.5) and tied for the league lead in forced fumbles (five). (Spencer Brown, Buffalo’s starting right tackle, is doubtful with an ankle injury.) Buffalo’s last two wins, 36-10 over the Ravens and 23-6 in Minnesota, were its two biggest of the season, and the defense gave up 16 points across both. That unit had allowed 29 or more points in five of its first six games, so the last two weeks matter. The question mark is the quarterback list: Carson Wentz, and a Ravens group that got one pass from Lamar Jackson. Geno Smith isn’t a world beater by any means, but he is an experienced starting QB in this league, with some real young talent around him. If they’re allowed to get hot and enjoy the game, it can turn into a tough afternoon for Buffalo very quickly. Without further ado, here are the players I believe will need to be at their best so the Bills can earn their eighth win of the season: KEEP ROLLING James Cook, RB: If you feed him, he’ll come James Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards and a touchdown in Minneapolis, 10 more carries than any other running back in Week 9. He averaged 2.7 yards per carry through three quarters behind Tylan Grable and Austin Corbett on the left side, then the Vikings’ front wore down: 47 yards on one fourth-quarter possession that ended with his five-yard touchdown, and Buffalo held the ball for 42:32 to Minnesota’s 17:28. PFF still graded him 52.9, a reminder that the yardage came on volume more than clean running. The Jets are the kind of defense volume works against. They rank 26th against the run at 128.0 yards per game, and it is getting worse: about 118 per game through five weeks, just over 140 over the last four. Kansas City ran for 163 yards at 5.1 yards per carry last Sunday. The advanced numbers disagree on the details, so I’ll flag it: the Jets are ninth in EPA per rush allowed (-0.142), which strips out garbage time, yet 30th in rush success rate allowed (51.5 percent). That reads to me like a defense that gives up steady, unspectacular gains, and those add up late. On the other hand, Cook is fifth in the NFL with 814 rushing yards, tied for eighth at 4.8 per carry, and he has scored in seven straight games. Since 2021, the Jets have allowed the Bills 145 rushing yards per game, 4.6 per carry, and 15 touchdowns across ten meetings, per the Jets’ own site. The one thing that can interrupt this is the football itself. That same site notes Cook has fumbled ten times since the start of last season (I flagged it in Week 6), and Bailey’s five forced fumbles lead the league. If Cook holds on to it, I expect a 25-carry day that gets better as it goes. Ed Oliver, DT: Win the one-on-ones Deone Walker gives you Ed Oliver has played five games this season, and the defense looks different with him in them. Through the first stretch, Buffalo allowed 25.3 points per game with him on the field and 31.7 without; in the two games since his return, it allowed 10 and 6. In Minneapolis, he played 28 snaps (58 percent), had three quarterback hits and graded 79.1 at PFF, the fifth-best mark on the defense. A PFF-based breakdown from The IDP Show has him at 11 pressures over those two games with no sacks and a 72.1 pass-rush grade for the season. Oliver has been around for a while now, but something has changed — Deone Walker, the nose tackle, was double-teamed on 71 percent of defensive snaps while Oliver was out, and he has earned the attention with an 86.1 PFF pass-rush grade (second among 126 qualifying interior linemen), 25 pressures and a spot on PFF’s midseason All-Pro second team. His run-defense grade is 61.9, 41st at the position, but the eye test certainly gives me some “he’s been better than this” vibes. With Breece Hall back from his quadriceps injury (15 carries for 61 yards last week) and Braelon Allen fourth in the league in rushing yards over expected (+124) and sixth at 5.0 per carry, I expect the Walker-Oliver combo to be at their best on Sunday. STEP UP Tylan Grable, OT: Back on the right side, with Bailey ahead Spencer Brown did not practice Thursday or Friday and is doubtful. I expect Grable at right tackle, with Dawkins back at left tackle and Anderson at left guard; Dawkins (ribs) and Anderson (ankle) both practiced fully on Friday and carry no designation. Right has been his best side. Before Minneapolis, most of his work had come there, including 82 snaps against Baltimore in his first real start, where charting-based metrics hit him with two pressures on 42 pass-blocking snaps, both in true pass sets. Against the Vikings, he moved to left tackle for all 80 snaps, and PFF graded him 51.0 overall with a 40.2 pass-blocking grade and four pressures allowed. PFF had him at 55.8 for the season over 133 snaps before that game. Bailey is the problem, though. He has 40 pressures on 194 rushes (20.6 percent, second-highest among players with at least 100), plus the sacks and the forced fumbles. PFF is less impressed by how he wins: a 10.3 percent pass-rush win rate (56th of 91 edge rushers) and a 66.0 pass-rush grade (38th). That gap suggests a rusher who finishes plays and benefits from the pressure around him more than one who beats tackles clean every snap, which is a matchup a swing tackle can survive. Brady said the Jets move Bailey around the formation, so it could be more about quickly recognizing stunt games and where the pressure is coming from, than simply neutralizing the man lining up in front of you. Allen was sacked four times in Minneapolis, and the bar for Grable is keeping Bailey from ending drives: no sacks, and no strips that reach the ball. Amani Hooker, S: The best moment for a new safety to arrive The Bills sent a 2027 second-round pick to Tennessee on Tuesday for Amani Hooker and a fifth, after releasing C.J. Gardner-Johnson, and Hooker said Wednesday he would play Sunday. He arrives with five interceptions, tied for the NFL lead and the most of any safety, three of them against Joe Burrow in Week 8. PFF has him at 81.0 overall, 75.2 in coverage (10th among 100 safeties) and 83.9 against the run (10th), and he played 99 percent of the Titans’ snaps across seven games. Buffalo’s defense had six interceptions through eight games and allowed 238.8 passing yards per game, the fourth-most in the league, with 28 completions of 20-plus yards. He doesn’t need to be the savior, though. The timing helps. The defense has allowed 10 and 6 points in its last two games, with six sacks over two weeks, and a new safety fits more easily on a unit that is already playing fast. Cole Bishop played all 48 snaps in Minneapolis, Damar Hamlin played 44, and Geno Stone 25, so the first thing to watch is who gives up snaps to Hooker. The test is Garrett Wilson, who leads the Jets with 527 yards and three touchdowns and practiced fully on Friday after a concussion, plus rookie Omar Cooper Jr. (306 yards and two touchdowns in five games, with an 83.3 percent catch rate. Jim Leonhard said the Jets create clean pictures for Smith and get the ball out. A safety with Hooker’s range and run-defense grade is supposed to muddy those pictures and shrink the explosive plays, and if he does it in his first game, the case for the trade makes itself. HONORABLE MENTIONS Also Rolling Connor McGovern, C: PFF graded him 75.5 in Minneapolis, fourth-best on the offense, with Dion Dawkins and Alec Anderson both out against the league’s heaviest-blitzing defense. The Jets rank fifth in pressure rate, and McGovern was limited Wednesday and Thursday with a neck injury before a full practice Friday and no designation. Ty Johnson, RB: Johnson played only 17 snaps (21 percent) and still graded 79.0, third-best on the offense, with a 36-yard catch on a third down early in the third quarter. He has 17 catches for 210 yards in six games, and against a defense that sends extra rushers, he should have more opportunities to produce. Khalil Shakir, WR: Shakir caught all four of his targets for 58 yards (PFF: 80.1, second-best on the offense). Over his last five games, he has 23 catches on 27 targets for 318 yards. The Jets lean on man coverage, and Shakir is Josh Allen’s quick answer when the rush arrives. Dorian Williams, LB: Williams played just 19 snaps (40 percent, down from 29 a week earlier) and graded 92.8, second on the defense behind Terrel Bernard’s 94.9. His interception came with T.J. Hockenson covered one-on-one down the seam, his second of the season after the one against the Raiders in Week 6. I had him in a different corner of this list for coverage that week, so the play stood out. The Jets use four tight ends (Kenyon Sadiq, Mason Taylor, Jeremy Ruckert and Jelani Woods), and that is his test. FINAL THOUGHTS Aaron Glenn is 0-8 against AFC East opponents as Jets head coach, and Brady is right that New York has played in plenty of one-score games. I’d like to see a more pass-happy approach built on Allen’s playmaking ability, like in the first couple of games. It could result in a blowout win, with the Jets struggling to keep up with the most prolific offense in the league. However, that approach got Allen banged up real quick, so I expect Brady to keep riding Cook and the run game until the Jets really force Superman to put the cape on. On defense, Oliver and Walker will have to squeeze the pocket, and Hooker can make an impact on the safety group for the first time. The risk sits on a talented divisional rival, playing at home, putting together a strong game against the AFC leaders who could overlook them. Which worries you more on Sunday: Grable against Bailey, or something else? Tell me in the comments! Catch up on all this and more with the latest edition of Leading the Charge!

stories.title: The 2nd quarter of Texans vs. Chargers cost safety Jalen Pitre $30k
stories.summary: Jalen Pitre’s wallet is a LOT lighter after the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.
stories.detailText: Photo by Karl Anderson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jalen Pitre was hit with not one, but two big fines for his play against the Chargers in Week 9. Pitre owes the league $30,800 for unnecessary roughness/use of the helmet on two separate plays. Both plays occurred in the second quarter of the Texans’ 44-22 win over the worst team in the NFL right now. On the first, at 8:58, Pitre’s fine for use of the helmet came on a tackle of Chargers WR Tre Harris on third-and-goal for a 7-yard loss. The play forced the Chargers to settle for a field goal. The second play, with :25 left in the first half, was a tackle on Chargers TE Charlie Kolar for a 5-yard game. Pitre was not flagged for either play during the game. Pitre has been fined three previous times in his NFL career for a total of $43,351, and the two fines from Texans vs. Chargers are his first since Jan. 2024. On the Chargers side, cornerback Donte Jackson was fined $12,537 for unnecessary roughness/striking, kicking, or kneeing for a play in the fourth quarter of Texans vs. Chargers, a Woody Marks carry for no gain. stories.title: Saints RB Travis Etienne Jr. activated off IR for game vs. Panthers
stories.summary: The New Orleans Saints activated running back Travis Etienne Jr. off injured reserve prior to their game against the Carolina Panthers, the team announced Saturday.
stories.detailText: NEW ORLEANS -- The New Orleans Saints activated running back Travis Etienne Jr. off injured reserve prior to their game against the Carolina Panthers , the team announced Saturday. Etienne has been on IR since Oct. 1, following a hamstring injury that occurred in a Week 3 game against the Las Vegas Raiders . Etienne had been dealing with hamstring issues in the week leading up to the Raiders game. Though he rushed for a season-high 57 yards, he left the game in the third quarter after grabbing his left hamstring at the end of a 16-yard run. Etienne said he "feels great," and said he was eager to return after practicing fully on Friday. "I definitely want to, but I mean, whatever they require me, what I'm going to do. So I'm just here to help the team and I feel like not much help when I'm out there on the sideline in my street clothes. So hopefully it let me suit up and I go out there and just be a valuable asset to the team," he said. Etienne will likely share carries with Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime , who led the team with 72 rushing yards vs. the Cleveland Browns last week after being claimed off waivers. The Saints also placed second-round pick Christen Miller on IR after he was downgraded earlier in the week with a knee injury. They will be without two starting offensive linemen against the Panthers as Erik McCoy (biceps) and Taliese Fuaga (knee) were both declared out Friday.

West (99) reacts after sacking Indianapolis Colts quarterback Philip Rivers (17) on Monday, Dec. 22, 2025, during a game at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The San Francisco 49ers were a bit quiet with their roster news for Saturday. Crawford was not flagged for the blindside block during the game. It’s his only fine so far in the 2026 season. The Cardinals selected Crawford in the seventh round of the 2025 NFL Draft. stories.title: Cowboys key matchup: Dallas WRs vs San Francisco 49ers CBs
stories.summary: The Cowboys wideouts could dictate the game on Sunday
stories.detailText: Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images | Getty Images Ahead of the 2026 season, all Dallas Cowboys fans had Week 10 circled. The Cowboys and San Francisco 49ers rivalry dates back to the 70’s, but recently the Cowboys have come up short more often than not. Heading into Week 10, the two teams are not playing on the same level. Sitting at 7-1 the 49ers are staring the NFC number one seed in the face, while the Cowboys are currently fighting for their lives to make the postseason. With both teams banged up and final injury reports issued , we can finally get an idea of what the key matchup for this contest will be, and the Cowboys best path to victory is pretty clear. The 49ers defense is currently seventh in the NFL in EPA/play and 14th in success rate, but their number one rush defense in the NFL helps weight those rankings. If the Cowboys are able to pull of a massive upset, the Cowboys will need to win through the air, early and often. Through nine weeks, the 49ers have the 12th-ranked defense in the league in terms of dropback EPA allowed and the 10th-ranked defense in the league in terms of success rate allowed. Despite ranking 20th in rushing success rate allowed, the 49ers rank first in rush EPA. With no clear path to running the football successfully, this game falls into the hands of CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Ryan Flournoy, and even KaVontae Turpin. With Pickens cleared to go, the Cowboys will be at full strength on offense for the first time in a few weeks, minus Jake Ferguson. On the other side of the field, the 49ers secondary is quite banged up. Starting cornerbacks Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green are questionable for the game, after both logging limited practices on Friday, after both being DNP’s on Wednesday and Thursday. Starting nickel Upton Stout is also questionable for the game after practicing in limited fashion all week. The 49ers are pretty thin from a depth perspective in the secondary if even one of their starting corners are unable to go, but if they end up missing multiple players, the Cowboys wide receivers should be able to dominate this matchup. Even if all three guys suit up, the Cowboys wide receivers can find plenty of wins against this unit. After sitting out last week, Pickens holds no injury destination heading into the game and seems to be near full strength for the first time in over a month. With Pickens back in the lineup and Turpin expected to return, the Cowboys should have their full complement of weapons to attack a banged up secondary of the 49ers. If the Cowboys want to upset the NFC favorites in Week 10, they will need all four of their starting receivers to impact the game in a big way, making this the key matchup to watch on Sunday.

Fuck this guy, man. Illegal substitution, defense. Too many men on the field. Half the distance to the 2 yard line, 2nd and goal. Offsides, Dylan Day. Half the distance. 3rd and goal on the 1. Offsides, defense (player unspecified). Half the distance. 4th and goal inside the 1. Team Grades Offense: B- The counting numbers for yards got real big, and the points got to a nice place, but Miami left tons of meat on the bone and points on the field today. This should have been a 50 burger easy. Settling for 3 FGs, dropping a pick-6 (not on the offense, but still matters to the point total), some bad OL play, and a passing game that was effective but lacked explosion are all factors affecting this grade. On the flip side, 36 points 532 yards and a win on homecoming over a team looking for revenge on multiple levels who had just won their previous 2 games by a combined score of 88-5 is pretty damn good. Still, we’ll need to be better to accomplish our goals, so this is the grade. Defense: C- Look. Nate Sheppard is good, but he’s a 1 man team. Allowing him to go crazy the way we did/he did is just bad. Holding Duke to 4 scores on 9 offensive possessions is good, but I’d like that number to be lower. Miami was robbed of a turnover on one drive where the player who fumbled didn’t even try to say he didn’t, but the refs gave Duke the ball, and the Blue Devils went with tempo so there was no chance for a review. If that, and the last touchdown, come off the board, I’d have felt better with 10-13 points allowed being the result. But it wasn’t. So I have to grade what happened. And I did. Special Teams: B+ 3/3 FGs. Great punts. Good coverage. The only thing keeping this from being an A was the long KR on the kickoff from the 20 after the Lofton Unsportsmanlike penalty. When given room, opposing returners and return teams continually crease Miami’s kick coverage unit. I don’t like it. Oh, and the hands team for the final kickoff was prepared for an onside kick, and the returner (Fitzgerald) fielded the squibbed kick flawlessly to possess the ball and allow Miami to go with Victory Formation. MUCH better here. Coaching: B There were good moments and bad moments, but overall I think this was a strong showing. The coaches had the team dialed in and ready to compete, looking to bounce back from the Notre Dame loss. There was some lethargy early, and the offense took a while to get going, but the defense got 3 straight punts to start the game, so that’s good! The big thing here with the demerit were the penalties and lack of performance from the players. At a certain point, guys just need to make plays. That’s on the players, not the coaches. So for those who are reading this and thinking “OMG Shannon Dawson is stupid”, consider that for like the 6th game out of 10 this year, Miami had a penalty before the first offensive snap of the game. And consider, if you will, that he’s not calling plays with the intent of OL whiffing blocks. AND, also consider that Corey Hetherman is not designing his defense to intentionally and continually miss tackles. So, I say that to say that, coming off the Notre Dame loss, on Homecoming, at Noon, against a team that’d just won consecutive games by an aggregate 88-5, with a program whose coach and multiple staffers have personal grudges against Miami, this was a solid performance and 2 score win. I’ll take it. That’s it for this installment of The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly. Hop in the comments and share your thoughts. Go Canes

stories.title: Packers activate RB Chris Brooks, WR Skyy Moore
stories.summary: The Packers will have two offensive players back in the lineup for Sunday's matchup with the Vikings.
stories.detailText: The Packers will have two offensive players back in the lineup for Sunday's matchup with the Vikings. Running back Chris Brooks and wide receiver Skyy Moore were both activated from injured reserve on Saturday. Brooks ran 15 times for 70 yards in the first four weeks of the season and has missed five games with an ankle injury. Moore has also been out with an ankle injury and had seven catches for 35 yards in five appearances. Brooks provides depth in the backfield with Josh Jacobs out this week. Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd, and Pierre Strong are also on hand. The Packers made space for Brooks and Moore by placing tight end Josh Whyle on injured reserve and waiving wide receiver Coleman Owen.

stories.title: Jaguars Arik Armstead fined for hip-drop tackle vs. Ravens in Week 9
stories.summary: Arik Armstead wasn’t flagged for a hip-drop tackle on this play against the Ravens, but he will be fined for it.
stories.detailText: Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images | Getty Images Arik Armstead will be fined $17,911 for a hip-drop tackle in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Baltimore Ravens. The fine for unnecessary roughness stems from a tackle on Derrick Henry on the Ravens’ very first offensive play of the third quarter. The play was a direct snap to Henry, who was stopped after just 1 yard by Armstead and Matt Dickerson. Armstead was not flagged for the play at the time. The fine is Armstead’s second of the season, after being fined 11,941 for a face mask penalty when the Jaguars played the Patriots back in Week 3 of the 2026 season. Armstead was the only Jaguars or Ravens player who was fined for their Week 9 play. Armstead, who signed with the Jaguars in 2024 after spending the first nine years of his career with the 49ers, has 14 tackles, 1.5 sacks and a pass breakup for the Jags this season. Armstead had two tackles in the Jaguars’ 33-10 victory, including the one he was fined for against the Joe Fagnano-led Ravens in Week 9. The funds the NFL collects through fines are donated to the NFLPA’s assistance to retired players, and the NFL Foundation and other nonprofit organizations that support kids’ sports leagues, community wellness initiatives, and the safety, health and well being of athletes at all levels of sports.

stories.title: Chargers list Ladd McConkey as questionable for Monday night
stories.summary: Wide receiver Ladd McConkey is among the Chargers players listed as questionable for Monday night's game against the Ravens.
stories.detailText: Wide receiver Ladd McConkey is among the Chargers players listed as questionable for Monday night's game against the Ravens. McConkey is dealing with a back injury that kept him off of the practice field this week. McConkey has dealt with a number of injuries this season and has 17 catches for 286 yards and a touchdown on the season. The Chargers also listed guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe (ankle), tight end David Njoku (fibula), linebacker Denzel Perryman (pectoral), and offensive lineman Trey Pipkins (personal, knee) as questionable. Njoku, Perryman, and Pipkins will need to be activated from injured reserve in order to play against Baltimore. Wide receiver Brenen Thompson (hamstring) is considered doubtful while guard Branson Taylor (ankle), cornerback Isas Waxter (ankle), and safety Kendall Williamson (calf) have been ruled out.

stories.title: Michael Pittman Jr. says he feels healthy enough to return
stories.summary: The Steelers could soon be getting a boost to their receiver room.
stories.detailText: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers made no trades ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, despite a clear need at wide receiver. Although the Steelers were interested in Tennessee’s Calvin Ridley and Jacksonville’s Brian Thomas Jr., a trade never materialized. While the receiver room has a bleak outlook right now, one of the Steelers’ highest paid receivers seems close to making his return from injured reserve. Steelers veteran wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. has been out since Week 4 after suffering a plantar fasciitis injury. Still, it seems like his return could come sooner rather than later. “It feels good, and today was probably my best day yet,” Pittman told Brendan Howe of Steelers Now on Thursday. “Yesterday was good, today was even better, so definitely trending the right way.… I would love the opportunity to play this week, but that’s out of my control. I definitely let them know today that I thought it was good.” Pittman Jr. remains on injured reserve, with the Steelers yet to open his 21-day practice window. The receiver was seen working off to the side this week and even ran during warmups. Although Pittman Jr. will be out this week against Cincinnati, the receiver feels healthy enough to go. The Steelers acquired Pittman Jr. in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts this past March. The receiver has appeared in just three games so far this season, recording seven catches for 89 yards in those contests. Let us know what you think in the comments . stories.title: NFL Week 10 Injury Report: Kenneth Walker ruled out, Rhamondre Stevenson listed questionable
stories.summary: Track the injuries to know around the NFL, all in one place.
stories.detailText: Staying up to date on NFL injury news is of the utmost importance for fantasy football success. The article below tracks all fantasy-relevant players currently listed on their team's injury report and provides fantasy managers with actionable recommendations as new information rolls in. Check back for updates from Tuesday through Saturday. Don’t forget: Check out the Rotoworld player news feed for all the latest news, notes, and transactions around the league. **UPDATED AS OF SATURDAY, NOVEMBER 14 AT 4:30 PM ET** AFC East ◆ Buffalo Bills Dalton Kincaid - TE (ankle) Kincaid was limited but was removed from the injury report Friday . He will play against the Jets. Impact: Likely none. Kincaid has played through injuries this season largely without issue. Joshua Palmer - WR (hamstring) Palmer managed only seven offensive snaps in Week 8 before departing with an aggravation of the hamstring injury he has battled since Week 4. He was placed on injured reserve. Impact: Not much, honestly. Palmer has played sparingly this season in a situational role, although his absence could leave room for Skylar Bell to be active for the third time this season. ◆ Miami Dolphins De’Von Achane - RB (knee) Achane suffered a torn ACL in the team's Week 3 loss to the Chiefs, ending his season. Impact: Achane's unfortunate season-ending injury creates opportunity for Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright . The timing of the injury makes it likely that Achane is able to fully recover before the start of the 2027 regular season. Malik Willis - QB (groin) The Dolphins placed Willis on injured reserve in Week 10. He will be eligible to return in Week 14, but Willis is seeking a second opinion after the injury progressed into his abdomen. Season-ending surgery is possible . Impact : Kyle McCord 's installation as the team's starter hurts all involved. Until we see how McCord fares in this system, only Ollie Gordon is a safe FLEX starter. Chris Bell - WR (knee) Bell is listed as doubtful for Week 10 against the Colts. Impact: Bell has largely been unable to get anything going during his rookie season, with the team leaning more heavily on Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas . The rookie's expected absence could afford Kevin Coleman Jr. additional opportunities, although the low-volume Miami pass offense remains unlikely to support more than one pass catcher, now playing with a backup quarterback in Kyle McCord . ◆ New England Patriots Romeo Doubs - WR (shoulder) Doubs was placed on injured reserve following a shoulder injury sustained in Week 6. He will miss the next four games, at minimum. Impact: The Patriots have now played only 33 offensive snaps with both Doubs and A.J. Brown on the field together this season after Doubs was injured on his second offensive snap in Week 6. Brown returned from injured reserve in Week 6 and should have the runway to return WR1 numbers while Doubs remains sidelined. A.J. Brown - WR (knee/ankle) Brown has missed the previous two weeks with a "flare up" in his knee. The team announced Tuesday that he will travel to Germany for Week 10. He was limited to begin the week before drawing the questionable tag for Week 10. Impact: DeMario Douglas , Kyle Williams , Mack Hollins , and Kyle Williams led the team in snaps and routes in the absence of Brown in Week 9, with none of the bunch consistent fantasy producers. Fantasy managers are likely forced to wait until late in the week to get a better sense of whether Brown will return in Week 10. TreVeyon Henderson - RB (illness) Henderson has been sidelined since Week 8 and will not play in Week 10 against the Lions. Impact: See below. Rhamondre Stevenson - RB (knee) Stevenson is reportedly set to miss "a short period of time" with a tendon issue in his knee, per ESPN's Adam Schefter . Even so, the veteran back drew the questionable tag for Week 10 against the Lions. Impact: An absence from Stevenson could place the team in a dire situation with TreVeyon Henderson also sidelined for an indefinite time, likely leaving Corey Kiiner atop the depth chart for a matchup against the Lions in Germany. Kiner would gain viable FLEX status, should Stevenson miss. Lan Larison is his backup. Hunter Henry - TE (foot) Henry played through this injury in Week 9, and was limited to begin Week 10. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Lions in Germany. Impact : He is a TE2 against the Lions. ◆ New York Jets Garrett Wilson - WR (concussion) Wilson was ruled out for Week 9 Friday after failing to practice all week with a concussion. He was limited to begin Week 10, and head coach Aaron Glenn said he is "very hopeful" that Wilson will play . He officially drew the questionable tag for Week 10. Impact: Adonai Mitchell could operate as the Jets' No. 1 wide receiver in his albeit volatile downfield role. Omar Cooper - WR (ankle) In Week 9, Cooper injured the same ankle that he hurt earlier this year, but he practiced in a limited capacity to begin Week 10. Despite drawing the questionable tag, he is expected to play. Impact: Cooper is on track to play and warrants FLEX treatment against the Bills. Adonai Mitchell - WR (knee) Mitchell is listed as questionable for Week 10 but is expected to play. Impact: Minimal. The downfield threat brings a wide range of outcomes on a weekly basis and makes for one of the more "yolo" starts in fantasy circles. AFC North ◆ Baltimore Ravens Lamar Jackson - QB (thumb) Jackson returned from an ankle injury in Week 8 and made it all of one offensive snap before suffering a thumb injury that is likely to sideline him for the remainder of the regular season. Impact: Jackson's absence is the biggest hit to the fantasy value of alpha receiver Zay Flowers , who falls to a mid-range WR2 in rest of season rankings. Recent signee Jacoby Brissett is expected to start under center in Week 10 . Tyler Huntley - QB (toe) Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury in the team's Week 8 loss to the Bills. Impact: See above. Durham Smythe - TE (Achilles) Smythe suffered a torn Achilles in the team's Week 4 win over the Titans. His season is done. Impact: It was Matt Hibner who saw the largest increase in snaps following Smythe's departure in Week 4, making it unlikely we see veteran Mark Andrews in a more robust role. ◆ Cincinnati Bengals Andrei Iosivas - WR (thumb) The Bengals placed Iosivas on injured reserve in Week 3. The team activated his 21-day practice window this week but he is listed as doubtful to play in Week 10 against the Steelers. Impact: Wide receivers Colbie Young and Dohnte Meyers will duke it out for the No. 3 wide receiver role for at least the next four weeks. Meyers can be added in 14-team leagues, though his upside is questionable. Erick All - TE (knee) All suffered a torn ACL in Week 7. He was placed on injured reserve Tuesday and will miss the remainder of the regular season. Impact: All loses yet another season in devastating fashion after suffering his third torn ACL. His absence could provide a slight uptick in snap rate and route participation for Mike Gesicki , although he will be a difficult weekly start for as long as both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins remain healthy. ◆ Cleveland Browns Harold Fannin - TE (groin) Fannin played through the injury in Week 9, but did not enter the box score until overtime. He was limited to begin Week 10 and removed from the injury report Friday. Impact: None. Denzel Boston - WR (toe) Boston did not practice to begin Week 10, ultimately drawing the questionable tag. Impact: Boston continues to deal with lower-leg injuries, but he played effectively last week. If he cannot face the Texans in Week 10, KC Concepcion and Fannin would benefit. Raheim Sanders - RB (hip) The Browns placed Sanders on injured reserve in Week 6 . Impact: He will be eligible to return after four games missed. ◆ Pittsburgh Steelers Michael Pittman - WR (foot) Pittman was limited on Wednesday before being seen using a scooter in the locker room after practice . It was then revealed that Pittman aggravated his foot injury. The Steelers placed him on injured reserve late in Week 5 . The Steelers did not open his 21-day practice window after their Week 9 bye. Impact: Pittman's potential return could lower Germie Bernard 's target share. Roman Wilson - WR (finger) Wilson departed in the second half of Week 5 with a finger injury and is reportedly looking at a multi-game absence. He was ruled out for Week 6 on Friday and placed on injured reserve on Saturday. Impact: See above. Pat Freiermuth - TE (illness) The veteran tight end was added to the injury report Saturday with an illness, listed as questionable . Impact: We expect Freiermuth to play through the illness despite the late addition to the injury report. Darnell Washington could be a name to keep on fantasy radars, should Freiermuth miss. AFC South ◆ Houston Texans Woody Marks - RB (knee) Marks was limited to begin Week 10 but was removed from the injury report Friday. Impact: Likely none. Tank Dell - WR (hand/shoulder) Dell was limited to begin Week 10 but removed from the injury report Friday. Impact: Dell led the team with nine targets last week. He may have his work slightly scaled back this week, but he remains FLEX-viable. Marvin Harrison Jr. - WR (hamstring) Harrison was limited to begin Week 10. He was ruled out Friday. Impact: Hamstring injuries can be tricky for wide receivers. Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson would mildly benefit with Harrison sidelined. Jaylin Noel - WR (toe) Noel suffered a turf toe injury in Week 7. The Texans placed him on injured reserve in Week 8. He is expected to miss the remainder of the regular season. Impact: Tank Dell and recent acquisition Marvin Harrison Jr. would be in line to benefit. Harrison should be added in 12-team formats. David Montgomery - RB (groin) Head coach DeMeco Ryans said in Week 5 that Montgomery is " week-to-week " with a groin injury. He remains sidelined early in Week 10 and was ultimately ruled out. Impact: Woody Marks is a low-end RB2/FLEX. Jawhar Jordan - RB (undisclosed) The Texans placed Jordan on injured reserve in Week 7 . Impact: Jordan prevented Marks from handling a full-time role in Week 6. Dare Ogunbowale will probably do the same while Montgomery is sidelined. Jayden Higgins - WR (knee) Higgins saw his 2026 season taken from him due to a torn ACL suffered in camp. Impact: It's a massive blow to a Texans team that was counting on Higgins taking another step forward in his Sophomore campaign. The team traded for Kayshon Boutte in the wake of the injury and then added Marvin Harrison Jr. in a deal with the Cardinals ahead of Week 6. ◆ Indianapolis Colts Alec Pierce - WR (heel) Pierce aggravated the injury that required offseason surgery in Week 2. The Colts placed him on injured reserve in Week 3 . He will attempt to avoid surgery by rehabbing his injured heel. Head coach Shane Steichen said he is unsure whether Pierce will play again this season . Impact: Tyler Warren is the de facto top option through the air for the remainder of the season. ◆ Jacksonville Jaguars Bayshul Tuten - RB (ankle/foot) Tuten played in Week 9's Thursday Night Football after failing to practice leading up to the game. He did not practice the following Wednesday but was removed from the injury report Friday and will play in Week 10. Impact: Tuten saw his workload managed in the second half of a blowout win but appears to have escaped without aggravating either injury. Fantasy managers will want to track his status coming out of the mini-bye. Chris Rodriguez - RB (hand) Rodriguez played through the injury in Week 9 and remained limited early in Week 10. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Titans. Impact : See above. Jakobi Meyers - WR (ankle) Meyers played through the injury in Week 9 and sat out the following Wednesday . He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Titans. Impact: Meyers is a touchdown-dependent FLEX. ◆ Tennessee Titans Carnell Tate - WR (shoulder) Tate remains sidelined following the Titans' Week 9 bye. He was ruled out for Week 10 Friday. Impact: This could be consequential. Chimere Dike stepped into the vacated role almost to a tee and brings viable FLEX upside in a pass-funnel matchup against the Jaguars. Tyjae Spears - RB (knee) As of Week 10 , Spears has been sidelined since Week 7. He is listed as questionable for Week 10. Impact: Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status 90 minutes prior to first kick. AFC West ◆ Denver Broncos Jaylen Waddle - WR (concussion) Waddle suffered a concussion in the team's Week 9 win over the Panthers. Impact: The team's Week 10 bye should afford Waddle enough time to return without missing a game. RJ Harvey - RB (knee) Harvey popped on the injury report Thursday with a knee injury and was ruled out for Week 8 on Friday. He was placed on injured reserve Saturday and will miss the next four weeks, at minimum. Impact: Jonah Coleman is an RB2, operating as the team's starter. ◆ Kansas City Chiefs Kenneth Walker - RB (groin) Walker was added to the injury report Friday after missing practice with groin tightness, ultimately ruled out for Week 10 against the Falcons. Impact: Walker's absence shocks the fantasy landscape for Week 10, with Emmett Johnson now in line to serve as a true workhorse back in a run-funnel matchup against the Falcons. Fantasy managers will want to add and start Johnson immediately as a viable RB2 with RB1 upside. Patrick Mahomes - QB (elbow) Mahomes suffered an elbow injury to his throwing arm in the team's Week 9 win over the Jets. He is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Falcons. Impact: Pain management could lead to reduced throwing volume for Mahomes. Backup quarterback Justin Fields ( neck ) is practicing in full as well. Tyquan Thornton - WR (ankle) Thornton suffered a devastating ankle injury due to a hip-drop tackle in Week 4. He is reportedly set to undergo surgery within the week and will miss 12-16 weeks. Impact: The team has lost all ability to attack downfield without Thornton, meaning our fantasy interest should be confined to those with expected volume. ◆ Las Vegas Raiders The Raiders emerged from their Week 9 loss to the 49ers absent any fantasy-relevant injuries. ◆ Los Angeles Chargers David Njoku - TE (fibula) Njoku is reportedly set to see his 21-day practice window opened in the coming days. He was limited to begin Week 10 before drawing the questionable tag. Impact: Minimal. The Chargers have been the most disappointing offense in the league through the halfway point of the season. Ladd McConkey - WR (back) McConkey reportedly experienced back spasms during warmups for Week 9 and ultimately did not play . He is listed as questionable for Week 10. Impact: McConkey would be a WR3 if active, although fantasy managers are likely better off making alternate arrangements considering the timing of the Chargers' game. Justin Herbert - QB (left hand) Herbert injured his non-throwing hand in Week 9. He is not on the injury report heading into Monday Night Football. Impact: Likely minimal. NFC East ◆ Dallas Cowboys Jake Ferguson - TE (ankle) Ferguson departed the team's Week 9 win with an ankle injury. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday that the veteran tight end is "expected to miss time." He was ruled out for Week 10 Friday. Impact: Brevin Span-Ford is on hand to handle primary tight end duties. He is not a recommended streaming option outside of the deepest leagues. George Pickens - WR (hamstring) Pickens missed Week 9 with a hamstring injury. He was limited to begin Week 10 before being removed from the injury report Friday. Impact: Back to business as usual for the Cowboys for their Week 10 showdown against the 49ers. Pickens is an upside WR3 in a difficult matchup on the perimeter. Malik Davis - RB (hip) Davis was placed on injured reserve and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Impact: The Cowboys released both Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah at roster cuts and now have only Emari Demercado on the active roster behind starter Javonte Williams . Expect Israel Abanikanda to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad for Week 2, while Williams appears likely to see all the work he can handle against the Commanders. Williams is a locked-in RB1. Tyler Goodson - RB (ankle/knee) The team sent Goodson to injured reserve Saturday. Impact: The Cowboys have struggled with depth in the backfield all season, which takes another blow in the absence of Goodson. Impact: Expect Sam Roush to serve as the team's TE2 for the remainder of the season, while second-year tight end Colston Loveland should continue his recent ascension back into TE1 territory. ◆ Detroit Lions Jared Goff - QB (chest) Goff's play may have been impacted by the injury in-game last week, though it is tough to say for sure. Impact: Beyond the football implications, it is good to hear Reed avoided any life-altering injuries in Week 2. The Packers designated him to return from injured reserve in Week 9 and he is listed as questionable for Week 10. Impact: See above. Jauan Jennings - WR (calf) See above. Impact: See above. Don’t forget: Check out the Rotoworld player news feed for all the latest news, notes, and transactions around the league. stories.title: Seahawks star Ernest Jones receives NFL’s heaviest fine of Week 9 for hitting Trey McBride
stories.summary: Jones gets the double whammy of being penalized in game and penalized financially after the game.
stories.detailText: After yet another penalty-heavy game involving the Seattle Seahawks, the fines have been issued to both Seattle and the Arizona Cardinals for illegal hits. Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV was docked $23,882 for illegal use of helmet on Cardinals tight end Trey McBride. Jones was flagged for the hit, but the punishment obviously didn’t stop there. Jones and Atlanta Falcons receiver Drake London had the largest fines of the entire week, both for illegal helmet use. Ernest Jones IV was fined $23,882 for illegal use of helmet on Trey McBride on Arizona's only scoring drive. Jones was flagged for unnecessary roughness on the play. pic.twitter.com/3gkIiRTqjf — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) November 14, 2026 For comparison, here is what London got fined for. Two biggest fines in Week 9: $23,882 each for use of the helmet for #Falcons WR Drake London and #Seahawks LB Ernest Jones. Here’s London’s. pic.twitter.com/SVOWcNPjRF — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) November 14, 2026 Meanwhile, Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon was fined ( again ) after his taunting penalty on McBride following Seattle’s game-sealing goal line stand. Officials erroneously said it was a roughness penalty when in fact Witherspoon did not touch McBride. This one will cost him $17,911. "I NEVER TOUCHED HIM" 🤣 Never change, Devon Witherspoon pic.twitter.com/XREUMWhdsK — LG (@GridIronically) November 9, 2026 It’s Spoon’s second taunting fine this season and he’s certainly no stranger to taunting penalties and/or fines since entering the NFL in 2023. Seattle leads the NFL in accepted 15-yard personal foul penalties on the season , which includes taunting. As for the Cardinals, safety Kitan Crawford was fined $5,775 for an uncalled blindside block on Nehemiah Pritchett during a punt return. The NFL fined Cardinals safety Kitan Crawford (No. 36) $5,775 for a blindside block on Nehemiah Pritchett on a Seahawks 1st quarter punt. pic.twitter.com/WuWPmEYkBP — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) November 14, 2026 Jalen Sundell was notably not fined for his unnecessary roughness penalty on Zach Charbonnet’s big catch-and-run, which feels like an unofficial way to say that there should’ve been no flag on the play.

stories.title: Packers make 5 roster moves, don’t place Josh Jacobs on IR
stories.summary: TE Josh Whyle is going on the IR, while WR Coleman Owen was released
stories.detailText: (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers, as expected , had to make a couple of roster moves on Saturday to piece together a 48-man game-day roster for Sunday. Today, the Packers announced the activations of running back Chris Brooks and receiver Skyy Moore from the injured reserve. To make room for those additions on the 53-man active roster, Green Bay placed tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) on the injured reserve and released receiver Coleman Owen. On top of these moves, the Packers also elevated tight end Drake Dabney from the practice squad for a second consecutive week. Brooks gives Green Bay five running backs on their 53-man roster at the moment, as Josh Jacobs, who had surgery on his broken finger on Saturday, was not placed on the injured reserve. Jacobs will miss Sunday’s game against the Minnesota Vikings, meaning the Packers are likely to carry three of their four healthy running backs — Brooks, MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong Jr. and Kaleb Johnson — into tomorrow’s action. Moore is a slot receiver and a returner, the latter being a role that Owen filled while Moore was on the IR. Moore took over as the Packers’ starting slot receiver once Jayden Reed had his season-ending neck injury. Moore was later replaced by Savion Williams. It will be interesting to see if Moore takes over in the slot this week or if Williams will continue in that spot. Below is the full breakdown of the Packers’ 54 roster options going into Week 10: QB – 2: Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor RB – 5: Josh Jacobs, Chris Brooks, MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong Jr. and Kaleb Johnson WR – 6: Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, Skyy Moore, Savion Williams, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant TE – 4: Tucker Kraft, Mark Redman, Jonnu Smith and Drake Dabney OL – 11: Jordan Morgan, Aaron Banks, Sean Rhyan, Laken Tomlinson, Anthony Belton, Kevin Zeitler, John Williams, Travis Glover, Mekhi Becton Sr., Jager Burton and Donovan Jennings DL – 5: Karl Brooks, Devonte Wyatt, Chris McClellan, Jordon Riley and Anthony Campbell EDGE – 4: Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Brenton Cox Jr. and Dani-Dennis Sutton LB – 5: Zaire Franklin, Isaiah McDuffie, Ty’Ron Hopper, Nick Niemann and Kristian Welch CB – 5: Keisean Nixon, Brandon Cisse, Carrington Valentine, Benjamin St-Juste and Kamal Hadden S – 4: Xavier McKinney, Evan Williams, Javon Bullard and Kitan Oladapo K – 1: Trey Smack P – 1: Daniel Whelan LS – 1: Matt Orzech Green Bay has already ruled out the following players against Minnesota: RB Josh Jacobs (finger) C Sean Rhyan (ankle) On top of that, linebacker Zaire Franklin is doubtful to play (fractured shin — didn’t practice this week), and these players are questionable: RB Chris Brooks (ankle) S Javon Bullard (ankle/knee) OL Travis Glover (knee) S Xavier McKinney (foot) WR Skyy Moore (ankle) EDGE Lukas Van Ness (back) G Kevin Zeitler (ankle/triceps) Based on the roster math — post-Jacobs and Rhyan — the team has 52 options to make up their 48-man game-day roster. Two more offensive linemen will be ruled out, as Green Bay generally keeps eight up on the game-day roster. That gets us down to 50. Add Franklin to that, and it’s 49. Scratching whoever is the fourth running back in the pecking order gets us down to the game-day 48. That’s probably the scenario we’re looking at for Sunday. Assuming that the questionable players (outside of potentially the offensive linemen) are going to suit up against the Vikings. If that were not the case, the Packers probably would have used a second practice squad elevation this week.

stories.detailText: The Buffalo Bills have made a few internal transactions ahead of their Week 10 game against the Jets inside MetLife Stadium. And each of these moves come with some intrigue: Roster moves: – Activated DB Jordan Hancock from Injured Reserve – Released DB Te’Cory Couch – Elevated QB Shane Buechele from the practice squad — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 14, 2026 Hancock had a tremendous summer at training camp and the preseason but has been out since Week 2 with what clearly was a pretty serious hamstring injury. Suddenly, the Bills have plenty of safety depth in their secondary. As for Couch, this was somewhat of a surprising release given how well he played against the Ravens in Week 8. Because he’s still within his first four years in the NFL, he’s subject to waivers. If Couch clears waivers, the Bills will have the opportunity to place him back on their practice squad. As for the Buechele elevation — there’s no indication Josh Allen nor Kyle Allen are dealing with injuries. But now Buechele can be designated the emergency third quarterback, even if he’s inactive. Are the Bills attempting to get him a game check? I really don’t know. Your guess is as good as mine there.

stories.title: Badgers embarrassed by Maryland for second straight year
stories.summary: The Badgers had a fourth quarter collapse on Saturday.
stories.detailText: COLLEGE PARK, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 14: Ryan Hopkins #10 of the Wisconsin Badgers drops back to pass in the second quarter against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium on November 14, 2026 in College Park, Maryland. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers suffered an embarrassing 24-21 loss to the Maryland Terrapins for the second year in a row, once again raising questions about Luke Fickell and the direction of the program after the 31-10 win over Rutgers last weekend. Wisconsin entered the week on a strong note, as they had dominated Rutgers in true freshman quarterback Ryan Hopkins’s first start last weekend. They came into the game as 8.5-point favorites and were still in the mix in the Big Ten race with a 6-3 record and 4-2 conference record. However, just like last weekend, the Badgers suffered a surprising loss. A season ago, Wisconsin was embarrassed 27-10 on their own home field, which sparked a six-game losing streak. This season, it was a 24-21 loss to one of the worst teams in the Big Ten this season. Wisconsin opened the game on a high note, forcing a quick three-and-out on the first set of plays, while responding with a five-play, 57-yard touchdown drive. The Badgers got great field position and took advantage with a 21-yard Jaylon Domingeaux catch, a pass interference call, and a 17-yard Darrion Dupree run, leading to a four-yard touchdown run on the next play. The Badgers allowed one first down on their next set of plays, but quickly forced a punt again and seemed to be picking up where they left off a week ago. But on 4th & 1 at their own 39-yard line, they decided to go for it with a fullback dive, and Ryan Schwendeman fumbled. Clearly, the Badgers didn’t feel like a quarterback sneak was an option, and there was the lane to convert, but the fumble gave Maryland great field position. Credit goes to the defense, though, who got help from the Terrapins with two false starts to force a quick three-and-out and get the ball back on a punt, albeit at Wisconsin’s own 1-yard line. The Badgers went to Bryan Jackson twice, getting nothing, before a short pass on fourth down forced them to punt deep in their own territory. Once again, Maryland got great field position, even with a penalty at the end of the punt, starting at their own 47-yard line. But the defense was stellar again, as it had been throughout the first quarter, and Maryland opened the second quarter with a missed 51-yard field goal. Finally, the offense got some rhythm. Abu Sama, who was nowhere to be found in the first quarter, ripped an 18-yard run on his first touch, and Darrion Dupree followed that up with eight and 11-yard runs later in the drive to set up two more first downs. The Badgers got themselves in the red zone, but what has killed them all season hurt them again: a negative play on first down. That ended up derailing the drive, and they were forced to settle for a field goal. Midway through the second quarter, the defense had their worst drive of the game so far. Without a pass rush affecting the quarterback, Cardell Williams ripped off six straight completions before a quarterback keeper for one yard ended up in the end zone. Suddenly, a game where the Badgers defense had dominated through the first 20+ minutes was 10-7 with three minutes left in the half. Wisconsin went nowhere on its next drive, as Sama got just two yards before an incompletion and a sack on second and third down. So, the Badgers quickly punted, and Maryland got a great opportunity to tie the game up before halftime. Once again, it was a ton of Cardell Williams, both with his arms and his legs, as Maryland’s backup quarterback moved the ball down the field in the two-minute drill. Starting at Wisconsin’s 40-yard line, the Terrapins had four rushes and two passes, getting all the way down to the one-yard line. But Matt Jung and Mason Posa forced a huge fumble on a one-yard carry, recovering the ball before halftime and saving a touchdown. Unfortunately, Jung was carted off with a leg injury, needing a cast on his foot. The Badgers started with the ball in the second half, but their offense remained lifeless with another three-and-out, starting with a negative play. It really felt at this point that Jeff Grimes had no faith in his quarterback. The Badgers went screen (for -1), run (for five), and screen (for -2) for a three-and-out. The defense bounced back from two shaky drives with a quick three-and-out, but the Badgers coughed it up immediately. After a first down drop, Darrion Dupree took the second-down handoff and fumbled after no gain, with Maryland recovering and returning it to the Wisconsin 16-yard line. Four runs later, the Terrapins were in the end zone with a surprise 14-13 lead. Now, there was still a ton of ball game left, but Wisconsin’s offense looked shattered, and they needed a turnaround fast with injuries piling up on the defensive side. And it didn’t look good at first. The Badgers got no gain on first down, one yard on a second-down screen, and nothing on third down for a quick three-and-out. But Sean West was roughed on the punt, giving Wisconsin a free 15 yards. That, plus an unsportsmanlike conduct, took the Badgers from their own 31 to the Maryland 39. From there, Wisconsin went with five straight dropbacks, completing just one for 15 yards, which set up an easier field goal for Gavin Lahm from 41 yards, cutting the lead to 14-13. Maryland’s next drive was instantly killed by a false start and a holding penalty on the first two plays, and they quickly punted, with the Badgers getting the ball at their own 43-yard line. Well, Wisconsin finally started to get a rhythm and consistently move the ball, with Ryan Hopkins having a couple of nice scrambles and Jeff Grimes mixing in an end around. The Badgers quickly moved into the red zone after a 28-yard Hopkins run and, two plays later, punched it in from the one-yard line for a Darrion Dupree touchdown. Despite how poorly their offense had played, the Badgers were back on top, and they went for two to make it 21-14 at the top of the fourth quarter. Maryland’s offense was able to move a bit on its next drive, thanks to a 13-yard run from DeJuan Williams on 4th & 1 and a 15-yard penalty on backup safety Matthew Traynor, but its own holding penalty killed a very promising drive, as they punted in plus territory once again. With 8:43 left, the Badgers started with the ball on their own 10-yard line. This felt like the perfect time for them to kill clock and start to move the ball a bit offensively. They didn’t get a single yard, punting in less than a minute, and Maryland was in position to tie things up with 7:45 left. Well, penalties were the Terrapins’ Achilles ‘ heel. As their run game started to get going and they advanced to the Wisconsin 35-yard line, another unsportsmanlike conduct penalty came. Maryland didn’t recover and, once again, punted in plus territory. With 4:29 left on their own 20-yard line, could this be the drive for the Badgers to seal the deal? Darrion Dupree got five on the first play, but was stuffed on 2nd & 5. Then Ryan Hopkins fumbled a third-down snap, sending the Badgers back and forcing their fifth three-and-out of the game. Sean West’s punt went just 35 yards to midfield, which the Terrapins returned to the Wisconsin 39. One play later, the score was tied, as Cardell Williams hit Preston Howard for a 39-yard catch-and-run touchdown. Wisconsin had a ton of opportunities to close the game, and they never capitalized. But the game wasn’t over, as the Badgers had the ball with 2:11 left and all their timeouts. Things started great as Darrion Dupree took a screen 15 yards to get the Badgers a 1st & 10 at their own 40 at the 2-minute warning. Well, disaster struck after that, as Ryan Hopkins didn’t identify a free rusher and was crushed by the blitzer, fumbling and getting hurt in the process. So Maryland had the ball on the Wisconsin 33-yard line, needing just a field goal to take the lead. They ran the ball six times, getting one first down before kicking a field goal on 4th & 1 at Wisconsin’s 12, securing the 24-21 lead. The Badgers had just 29 seconds left with no timeouts and Colton Joseph in the game off the bench. Joseph committed an illegal forward pass on his first play, essentially sealing the game for the Badgers, and Wisconsin would go on to suffer its fourth loss of the season. This was an ugly one for the Badgers. The offense compiled just 201 total yards, going 2 of 12 on third downs, as Ryan Hopkins had a rough day, averaging 3.5 yards per pass. They also committed three turnovers, gifting Maryland some great field position. Defensively, the Badgers played well enough to win. They stopped the run, and the Terrapins went 2 of 13 on third downs. But they allowed Cardell Williams to get too comfortable in the pocket, marking the third time this year they’ve done that to a backup quarterback (Iowa, UCLA). This is an embarrassing loss for the Badgers and one that requires some deep thinking about the direction of the program, given how inconsistent this team has been over the past few weeks.

stories.detailText: MIAMI GARDENS - NOVEMBER 14: Miami running back Javian Mallory (21) evades Duke safety Andrew Pellicciotta (35) while carrying the ball in the first quarter as the Miami Hurricanes faced the Duke Blue Devils on November 14, 2026, at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Samuel Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Hurricanes beat the Duke Blue Devils today at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, FL, 36-25. Duke transfers Darian Mensah and Cooper Barkate had big games. The defense could not contain Blue Devils running back Nate Sheppard, but got off the field on a few third downs, plus forced a turnover. It wasn’t the prettiest game, but I’ll take it. Quick rant: I know Miami won the game, but man, the refs were extra awful today. There were multiple missed pass interference calls, the softest personal foul I’ve seen against Elija Lofton, and a blatant missed holding call against Armondo Blount in the red zone where the next play went for a touchdown. Today is why Miami Hurricanes fans talk about officiating as often as we do. Ugh. Let’s get to the three stars of the game. 1. Javian Mallory Miami’s stud freshman running back played his best game of the season today. Mallory is officially one of the most talented and trusted offensive players on the 2026 Miami Hurricanes roster. He looks like a replicant of Frank Gore. The way Mallory ran through Duke’s defense on the long catch-and-run touchdown as well as his fourth quarter 39-yard touchdown scamper. Oh, and Mallory picked up at least two linebacker blitzes head on, giving Mensah time to find a receiver. Coach Cristobal is lucky to have such a well-rounded running back behind Mark Fletcher Jr. Stats: 10 rushes, 71 yards, two touchdowns, three receptions, 79 yards, one touchdown. Freshman sensation Javian Mallory with another TD on the season. 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4arg0gAvVh — 247Sports (@247Sports) November 14, 2026 2. Darian Mensah The former Duke signal caller kept making plays today, despite his offensive line doing its best to provide as little protection as possible. Mensah was forced to scramble a ton. Luckily, his skill players did their part on catching the ball and making plays in the open field. Mensah only had the one touchdown pass to Mallory, but he made plenty of other quality throws. The play below was his highlight of the day in my opinion. Stat line: 30-41, 382 yards, one touchdown, zero turnovers, four rushes for seven yards. Love this dude. 7 rec 107 yards so far for Cooper Barkate pic.twitter.com/TMvm2nMUw3 — Grant Reacts (@GrantReacts1) November 14, 2026 3. Cooper Barkate The other high-profile Duke transfer had his second big game in a row post Malachi Toney’s injury. Barkate showed it all today: route running, hands, speed, strength, wiggle. He really does have it all as a receiver. He’s also faster than he looks. That 40-yard catch-and-run in the second quarter was impressive. It would be great to see Barkate finish with two more hundred-yard-plus games to close out the regular season. I love the way he is playing right now. Stats: 8 receptions for 134 yards. Cooper Barkate long catch and run! First Down Canes pic.twitter.com/GZXk3N4QlT — Grant Reacts (@GrantReacts1) November 14, 2026 Honorable mention: Xavier Lucas – He’s lucky that long touchdown pass on him in the fourth quarter didn’t count. (Sigh). Besides that, Lucas had a huge interception early in the fourth quarter that helped seal the win. Mohamed Toure – Toure led the Canes in tackles today with 11 total, 10 solo. I know Sheppard abused Miami defenders today, but I liked the way Toure tackled in space overall, especially compared to other Canes defenders. Speaking of overall, Miami’s defense is overall frustrating as hell. I am sure Cam will take them to task in G/B/U, but damn. And where is Damon Wilson? I don’t see his name at all in the box score. Yikes. Who were your three stars of the game? Let us know in the comments below.

stories.summary: The Miami Hurricanes started off their home stretch of ACC games on the right foot, defeating former Canes head coach Manny Diaz and his Duke Blue Devils 36-25 on Saturday afternoon at Hard Rock Stadium. Former Duke QB Darian Mensah continued his Heisman Trophy campaign going 30/41 for 386 yards with a touchdown and n…
stories.detailText: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 14: Mark Fletcher Jr. #4 of the Miami Hurricanes celebrates a touchdown during the first half of the college football game against the Duke Blue Devils at Hard Rock Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Eston Parker/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images The Miami Hurricanes started off their home stretch of ACC games on the right foot, defeating former Canes head coach Manny Diaz and his Duke Blue Devils 36-25 on Saturday afternoon at Hard Rock Stadium. Former Duke QB Darian Mensah continued his Heisman Trophy campaign going 30/41 for 386 yards with a touchdown and no picks. Javian Mallory was an absolute dude, with 150 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns. Cooper Barkate had a huge day with eight catches for 134 yards. Mo Toure had a team-high 11 combined tackles. Miami and Duke started off slowly on the offensive side of the ball, with the teams trading off five punts between them in the first quarter. Miami opened the scoring with a 39-yard Jake Weinberg field goal early in the second quarter. Duke answered with a field goal 13 plays later. Miami finally found the end zone on a four-yard run by Mark Fletcher, Jr. who left the game with an apparent injury in the first half and did not return. A 40-yard Barkate catch and run was the big play of the drive. Duke answered on the following drive, and it was the uber-talented Nate Sheppard who broke free for a 47-yard touchdown right up the middle. Sheppard had a field day with 224 scrimmage yards and two scores. Miami would answer with a chip shot field goal shortly before the half for a 13-10 lead at the break. The Canes got the ball first and drove down the field thanks to a 33-yard run by Jordan Lyle. And it looked like for a second Elija Lofton finally had his nifty end zone catch he was denied last week. But his one-handed grab was made just after he touched out of bounds and was reversed after review and a field goal followed. Miami forced a punt near midfield, and minutes later, Mallory took a short pass and went 63 yards weaving through traffic and to the end zone for a touchdown and a 22-10 lead. The blocking was nifty on the play from the backfield down the field. And Shannon Dawson made a truly head-scratching call on the two-point conversion attempt with a designed run to Mensah. Mensah was clobbered just before the goal line and bent backwards. You simply can’t risk your QB like that. Duke would answer back five plays later, with Sheppard cutting left and past Miami’s defense and getting to the corner on a five-yard run before throwing the U down over his knee (not sure why people do this). Miami raised that U right back up on the following drive, which was a death march of over seven and a half minutes that took 17 plays and went 79 yards. Mallory tore through the line and across the goal line from two yards for a two-yard score. Three plays later, Xavier Lucas turned for the ball on a poorly thrown pass by Walker Eget, and the Canes secured their only takeaway of the game. Five plays later, Mallory broke free off the left side for a 39-yard touchdown, and church was officially out at 36-17. Duke would add some window dressing with a last second touchdown throw on fourth down with under 30 seconds left to close out the scoring. A win, and Miami can clinch a spot in the ACC title game if UNC can knock off Louisvile this evening.

teamStories.detailText: Although the Seattle Seahawks are set to be without several key starters against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10, they’ll get some much needed depth from two experienced veterans. The Seahawks elevated cornerback Trevon Diggs and offensive tackle Bobby Hart from the practice squad for Sunday’s game against the Raiders, they announced on Saturday . Both players already have suited up for Seattle this season. It marks the third (and final) consecutive elevation for Hart, who’s served as a depth piece behind swing tackle Josh Jones while OT Charles Cross continues to recover from a high ankle sprain he suffered in the team’s Week 7 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs. As for Diggs, he’s in line to make his fifth appearance of the year, with his last having come against the Kansas City Chiefs — where the longtime cornerback logged just six defensive snaps. With both Devon Witherspoon and Nehemiah Pritchett healthy, he’s once again unlikely to see a significant role, barring an injury. Despite both having made multiple appearances this season, neither has made a noticeable impact. The veteran lineman played his first three snaps of the season against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 and Diggs has recorded just one tackle across 27 defensive snaps. Given the Seahawks are also poised to be without QB Sam Darnold (quad, ribs), OG Quenton Nelson (knee) and DT Leonard Williams (stinger), it’s unclear why they opted to activate Diggs rather than add depth at a more significant position of need — especially considering there were several players waiting in the wings. While Seattle’s practice squad includes options at each position, none have spent an extended amount of the time with the team. The Seahawks signed OG Cordell Volson on Thursday, DT Cole Brevard two days prior and QB Adrian Martinez on Nov. 4, making it plausible the team didn’t feel any could make as much of an impact as a player like Diggs.
